# tsk

> tsk is a terminal task board for you and your agents: one shared queue, a TUI for you, a CLI for them.

On macOS/Linux, install with `curl -fsSL https://gettsk.sh/install.sh | sh` or `brew install smarzban/tap/tsk`. On Windows 10/11 ARM64 or x86-64, run `irm https://www.gettsk.sh/install.ps1 | iex` in a PowerShell window (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7); it selects the native architecture. Download the script first to use `-NoPathUpdate`, which leaves user PATH unchanged. Windows package-manager submissions and signing are not included yet.
If Herdr is on PATH, the installer asks to run `tsk setup herdr` on an interactive terminal; when agent skill roots are detected it also asks once to install the tsk skill. The install ends with a single `Done.` line pointing at the board (plus the Herdr board shortcut after an accepted Herdr setup) and one row per skipped ask (`tsk setup herdr`, `tsk setup`); a custom `TSK_INSTALL_DIR` skips the asks and says so. Homebrew prints the Herdr setup command as a caveat.
Herdr's board shortcut opens or focuses one board per workspace across its tabs, preserving its view and edits. Other workspaces stay untouched; boards share the same task store.
Details: https://gettsk.sh/docs/install.md
The board always shows every live task in Doing and Todo, grouped by project: the desk first, then each live project under a dim heading, task-number order inside each group. There is no scope picker or sort toggle. Inside Git, the cursor starts on the repo root's project's first row; quick-add goes to that project when it is live, otherwise to the desk (a `!p` token overrides). The board does not archive projects: use `tsk project archive <name or path>` and `tsk project unarchive <name or path>`. In `!p name`, `tsk add -p name`, and JSON plans, a bare project name must uniquely match a known project; a new project destination requires an existing absolute directory (`/…` or `~/…` on macOS/Linux, `C:\…` or `~\…` on Windows).
On the task page or the wide detail, `P` opens a parent picker (type to filter, Enter saves, Escape closes) and `U` clears the parent. Both act on the open task only, refuse while a draft has unsaved changes, and never change either task's status, scope, or children. The page shows the parent line before the steps (`not found · link kept` for a deleted or missing parent, whose UUID stays) and the direct children with a done count after them; board rows with children end in a dim `⊂done/total` count. Tab and arrows select the parent and child lines; Enter or a click opens that task without changing the list, Escape returns to the previous task, and Enter on `parent  none` opens the picker. Long picker titles wrap.
New tasks start with status `todo`. The board shows Doing, then Todo, grouped by project. Use `tsk list --todo` or `--doing` to filter. Task status is only `todo`, `doing`, or `done`; questions and Herdr execution status are separate. The board checks GitHub releases at most daily and shows a dim `vX.Y.Z available, run tsk update` on the status row; set `TSK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` to disable. Run `tsk update` to run the official installer for an installer-managed copy; on Windows a detached helper waits for the running executable to exit before replacing it. Existing Herdr registration and outdated installed agent skills are refreshed; when no agent skill is installed, an interactive update can offer the first-install skill setup. Homebrew copies print `brew update && brew upgrade tsk` instead.
Store format v10 adds the optional per-task `after` wait list (`tsk add/edit --after`, `--no-after`; `tsk status doing` refuses with `waiting-for-after` until predecessors are done) and changes no existing data. v9 adds the secret question kind and changes no data (a v8 binary refuses it). v8 removes the Task thread label from live and trashed tasks; v7 mapped `open`/`ready` to `todo`, `started`/`blocked`/`review` to `doing`, and kept `done`. Earlier migrations still run in order, including v5 batch undo and v6 optional parent_task_id UUID relationships. Migration keeps a `tsk.json.vN` original-version backup; trash gets an original-byte `trash.jsonl.pre-v8` backup before its first rewrite. History, undo, revisions, archive flags, steps, parents, and question references are preserved. `--thread`, list thread filters, the JSON `thread` field, and quick-add `!t` are gone; a non-null plan `thread` is an `invalid-item` refusal. Name a working Thread with a `Thread: <agent-name> <workspace-id> <tab-id> <pane-id>` notes line instead. Restore matched live/trash backups together for rollback; older binaries refuse the newer store.
Done tasks stay in `tsk.json` for one day (`TSK_DONE_KEEP_DAYS`), then move to `done/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` by UTC completion date; the board shows only live done tasks, `tsk list --done --history` adds the moved non-archived ones, `tsk list --archived` includes moved archived tasks and tasks in archived projects, and `tsk list T<n>` finds them. Moved tasks are read-only.

`N` tasks on the desk are human-only notices: four starter tasks on a first open, one `What's new in tsk` task after an upgrade. `tsk list` never shows them.
Press Shift+M to enter multi-select, then mark tasks with Space, shifted arrow keys, or a plain click and use the board's status, archive, or delete shortcut on the whole set. Shift+M again while the board owns input, an action, Escape, or a view change exits the mode and clears its session-only marks; removing the last mark alone keeps the mode active, and text entry keeps Shift+M as a capital M. Enter and edit remain cursor-only. Board rows show the number and title, then a bold `!` (an approval waiting on you) or `?n` (questions and findings waiting on you), then dim progress counts: `✓done/total` steps before `⊂done/total` children (`✓2/5 ⊂1/3`). Board-list titles and status lines each stay on one line, shortened with `…` when they do not fit; Enter opens the full title and notes with wrapping. Each task uses one line by default. A bold `×` marks a non-empty `Blocked:` notes line on any task not done, beside its existing question marks and progress counts; Enter shows the full reason. Press `v` with board-list focus to show or hide the second status line for this session (hidden on launch): a `Blocked: …` line on any task not done, bold as `blocked: …`; otherwise a `Now: …` line on a Doing task, dim. Keys are case-insensitive, a leading `- ` is allowed, and the first match wins. Recommended notes status card: `Now:`, `Next:` (optional), `Blocked:` (only while blocked), and `Done when:` first, each replaced in place, then reference lines (`PR:`, `Linear:`, `Issue:`, `CI:`, `Thread:`). The CLI keeps its own order. At 110 usable columns or wider, the board is always a list beside the selected task's detail: right arrow, l, or Enter focuses the detail, left arrow, h, or Escape returns to the list, and clicking a task updates the detail with list focus. On the detail or a task page, `J`/`K` opens the next or previous task in list order; a dirty draft refuses. Text entry keeps h and l as characters. Inside Herdr (`HERDR_ENV=1`) the board polls Herdr's agent list in the background about every 30 seconds and marks a Doing task stalled with a bold `↻` before its question marks when its notes have exactly one complete `Thread:` line, it has not changed for `TSK_STALE_MINUTES` (default 30), that exact pane's agent is not working or not live, and the session has not asked about it within that time. Clicking `↻` (or the palette's `check task's thread`) sends that thread an identifier-only Herdr prompt to update the task's status card with `tsk edit`. The top row's bold `↻ check` button, its board shortcut (see the Keys guide), or the palette's `check stalled tasks` sends the single live `lead-` agent (by Herdr name, or by terminal title for an agent Herdr lists without a name, prompted through its pane) one prompt listing every stalled Doing task and every Todo task, asking it to get each stalled thread's status card and start a thread for each Todo task that can proceed without asking the user (deploys and irreversible actions still ask). Nothing is written to the store and no status changes; the status row says what was sent or why nothing was (outside Herdr, no single live lead, no matching live pane).

Press `/` to filter the rows the board shows. Every whitespace-separated query term must match the title, notes, steps, or `T` number. `Enter` pins the query and returns input to board keys, while `Esc` clears the input or a pinned query first. Done rows show only while the done drawer is open; the closed DONE heading keeps the count of matching done tasks.

The quit shortcut exits from non-editor board surfaces, including task pages, Help, and pickers. Text entry keeps its editing behavior; save recovery must be resolved first. Unsaved drafts block quitting, including a draft parked in the detail column. Quit attempts preserve the pending save's failure message. Escape dismisses editors and overlays first, then returns detail focus to the list; task drafts stay parked. Escape then quits without confirmation at the list root. The browser demo releases keyboard focus at root instead of exiting. See the Keys guide for shortcuts.

On an explicit Agent board, `2` opens the questions tab: NEEDS APPROVAL, FOR YOU, FINDINGS, WITH LEAD, and CLOSED, with records without an audience shown apart as target unknown and left out of the tab number and row marks. `Enter` opens a record (side by side at 110+ columns). A record is answered with one form, like Claude Code's answer form: the question text, then numbered choices with the highlight on the first (or the recommendation). `↑`/`↓` or `j`/`k` move it, `Enter` picks the highlighted choice at once, `1`-`9` pick by number, and a click picks. A question with options lists them (a two-line option shows its label with the second line dim beneath; picking saves the label), then `Type something…`, then `Explain it first` (approvals and findings end with it too; it saves nothing and, inside Herdr, sends the one live `lead-` agent the single line `/wait-what Q<n>` so it explains the question before you answer). After `Type something…`: typing on that row (or `Enter`) opens an inline field, `Enter` saves the text, `Esc` leaves the field keeping the draft. A question without options opens on one focused field. An approval shows its exact terms above `1. Approve these exact terms`, `2. Reject`, `3. Add a comment…` (also `m`; `Enter` answers with the comment alone as `commented`, `Esc` keeps it to ride approve or reject; never itself an approval, never checked against the terms); Approve saves only when the terms and revision the page showed still match the snapshot and a fresh read, otherwise it refuses and rebinds to the new terms. A finding offers `1. Create the task and run it`, `2. Create the task only`, `3. Close`. Answered, closed, lead-addressed, and target-unknown records are read-only. `c` corrects, `t` opens the task, `r` resends a lead request, `J`/`K` step, `PgUp`/`PgDn` or the wheel scroll the page. A saved answer returns to the list with the cursor on the next waiting record; CLOSED is folded until `z`. A secret request (FOR YOU) shows its fnox key, profile, and config and opens on `1.` its masked field (`•` per character) plus `2. Reject`; `Enter` on the field runs `fnox set [-g | -c <config>] [--profile <p>] <KEY>` with the value on stdin only (`TSK_FNOX_BIN` overrides the binary), recording only the answer `set`; picking `2. Reject` (or `tsk ui-answer`'s `reject: true`) instead closes it with no value and no fnox call, recording `rejected`; a secret is never corrected, set, or rejected again. A fnox failure shows `fnox set failed`, saves nothing, and keeps it open. A finding offers create-and-run (a Doing task plus an identifier-only request to its `lead_recipient` when exactly one live agent has that name), create-only, or close, never creating a second task and never creating one in an archived project. Quitting is refused while an answer is typed or a question save is unresolved. The board shows `waiting on you  approval n · question n · finding n  → 2` when something waits, plus `target unknown n`. The task page lists the task's questions, findings, and `Linear:`/`PR:`/`CI:`/`Thread:` notes lines; a Thread line focuses a pane only on an exact single four-token live match. On the task page, bare `e` edits and bare `a` adds a step.

`tsk threads` opens a read-only Herdr view of live lead and issue-thread sessions, grouped only by Herdr execution status: BLOCKED, IN MOTION, ON DECK. It never reads or writes the task or question store. Inbox metadata is optional annotation only; it does not change grouping or indicate a wait for the user. See the Threads guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/threads.md

## For agents

- `tsk guide` prints the workflow; `tsk setup` detects agents and can install the skill; `tsk setup <agent>` targets one agent
- The skill covers rules of engagement, board language, the exit contract, and workflows, and points at `tsk help <command>` for syntax; its `Refine a task` section shapes a rough task into a brief on the board (propose, then write)
- `tsk list T<n>` returns the complete task, including notes and steps, in human-readable or JSON form; human output opens the steps block with `Steps: done/total done (percent%)`, and the task page's step heading reads `steps done/total · percent%`
- `tsk steps T<n> move <short-id> --before|--after <short-id>` (or `--first`/`--last`) reorders a step, keeping its short ID and checked state; `tsk steps T<n> add "…"` takes the same place flags. On the task page, a keyboard shortcut moves the selected step and adding a step with one selected puts it directly below
- `tsk list` groups Doing before Todo and orders Todo oldest capture first; Doing and Done use most recent status change first. This is separate from the board's project grouping. `--json` is that flat board order; with `--all`, human output groups each status by scope, ordering the groups by their first row and keeping the board order inside each group
- `tsk import linear` (needs `LINEAR_API_KEY`) creates a task per Linear issue, one way: title `<IDENTIFIER> <title>`, notes starting `Linear: <IDENTIFIER> <url>`, which also dedupes reruns. Filters `--team`, `--linear-project`, `--assignee`, `--state`, `--limit`; destination `-p` or `--desk`; `--update` refreshes title and status of existing copies; `--dry-run` writes nothing; `--json` prints a report. Missing key or Linear errors exit 1 with nothing saved. macOS and Linux only
- `tsk add --parent T10` and JSON plan `parent` strings select one parent; `tsk edit T12 --parent T10` replaces it, `--no-parent` clears it. `tsk edit T12 -p <project>` or `--desk` moves a task; the destination resolves like `add -p`. Self/cycles refuse. `tsk list T10 --json` includes direct parent/children and calculated Done/total counts; archived children count, deleted children/notices do not. Deleted/missing parents retain their UUID as unresolved; no state changes cascade.
- Linear import reads only the direct parent identifier/URL, keeps `Parent: Linear <identifier> <URL>` in new-task Notes, and links an existing or same-batch imported parent by UUID. No recursive import or later reconciliation. `--update` keeps user Notes and parent relation. External GitHub Notes use `Parent: GitHub <repo>#<num> <URL>`; GitHub intake is separate.
- `tsk ask --file question.json`, `tsk questions [Q-number|UUID] [--task T<n>]`, `tsk answer Q1 --file answer.json`, and `tsk route Q1 --file route.json` (set `audience` `user`/`lead` and `lead_recipient` under the same Q number, given `expected_revision`) require an explicitly selected non-personal Agent state directory (`--state-dir` or `TSK_STATE_DIR`). An approval answer may carry an optional `comment`: free text beside the `approve`/`reject` decision, refused on anything but an approval or when blank, and never itself an approval. They never fall back to the personal board. Questions preserve full text, Task/Q UUID separation, expected-revision CAS and append-only corrections. Shared `tsk.json` holds only shareable summaries/references; private question and approval originals stay in Git-excluded `questions-private/`. Answers persist before identifier-only Herdr notification; registration targets recipient and answers/corrections target origin Thread. Saved, notification failed, and durability uncertain are separate outcomes. Ordinary Agent/imported answers never issue user approval. Confirmed UI or verified original user-chat evidence binds approval to exact target/action/H-or-plan-digest/scope/rollback. No PIN, ACL, chmod protection, encryption or signature is added; same-OS-account UI impersonation is not prevented. `tsk answer` refuses UserUi origin. A secret question (`"kind": "secret"`, `"audience": "user"`, `"secret": {"key": "KEY", "profile": null, "config": null}`; config is an absolute path to an existing regular fnox.toml or null for global) is answered only in the board's questions tab, which hands the value to `fnox set`; the value is never stored or printed, `tsk answer` and `tsk ui-answer` refuse it with `secret-needs-board`, and the agent waits for answer `set`, then reads the value only through `fnox get`/`fnox exec` in its own process. `tsk ui-answer Q1 --file <json|-> --state-dir <dir>` is the user-input entrypoint for another interface (a Claude Code mod's ask prompt): it records origin `user_ui` from `expected_revision` plus exactly one of `choice` (option index), `text`, `approve` with the exact stored `approval` terms, or `reject` (an approval also takes a `comment` alone, saved as `commented`), through the same CAS, approval checks, and history; it prints one JSON line (`question_id`, `number`, `task_id`, `revision`, `status`, `notification`) and refuses with `tsk ui-answer: <code>: <message>` (`stale-revision`, `approval-refused`, `unknown-question`, ...). Agents never call it; any same-OS-user process could, so a Claude Code PreToolUse hook should refuse `tsk answer` and `tsk ui-answer` in every agent session but the Lead's. Full JSON and retry rules: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- Guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/agents.md
- CLI: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- `tsk help [<command>]` prints the CLI or one command's syntax reference.
- `tsk --version` (or `tsk -V`) prints the installed version.

Storage, backups, and release-check settings: https://gettsk.sh/docs/storage.md
- Full docs: https://gettsk.sh/llms-full.txt
